tagline: Neighborhood heat and air quality, calibrated and open.
locate-denied: Location not shared — search by name instead.
locate-unavailable: This device can't share a location — search by name instead.
overview-none-confirmed: No confirmed readings yet — all provisional this hour.
fresh-stale: This network may be behind — readings are not live.
map-hint: An interactive map of sensor locations — drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, or use the buttons and arrow keys. Each marker states its reading in text; the same data is in the List and Table tabs for any reader the map does not serve.
map-aria: Sensor locations. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, arrow keys to move.
headline-none: No confirmed air-quality readings for this hour yet — only provisional ones.
headline-worst: Worst confirmed air right now: {place} — AQI {aqi}, {category}.
guide-good: Air quality is good. It's a fine time to be active outside.
guide-moderate: Air quality is acceptable. Unusually sensitive people may want to take it easier on long or intense outdoor activity.
guide-usg: Sensitive groups — people with heart or lung disease, older adults, children, and teens — may feel effects and could shorten long or intense time outdoors. Others are less likely to be affected.
guide-unhealthy: Some people may feel effects; sensitive groups may feel more serious ones. Consider shorter or less intense time outdoors.
guide-vu: Health alert: everyone may feel effects. Sensitive groups should avoid outdoor exertion; others should limit it.
guide-haz: Health warning of emergency conditions: everyone should avoid outdoor exertion.
guide-source-heat: Heat context: US NWS heat index.
act-note: Practical steps drawn from US EPA and NWS guidance — not medical advice.
act-calm: No special heat or air precautions needed right now. Conditions can change fast — check back, and go by how you feel and official alerts.
act-heat-water: Drink water before you feel thirsty.
act-heat-shade: Take breaks in shade or air conditioning.
act-heat-easy: Avoid hard activity during the hottest hours.
act-heat-cool: Limit time outside and stay somewhere cool.
act-heat-signs: Watch for dizziness, nausea, or cramps — early signs of heat illness.
act-heat-neighbors: Check on older neighbors, kids, and anyone without air conditioning.
act-heat-ac: Get to air conditioning — a library, cooling center, or store all count.
act-heat-emergency: Hot dry skin, confusion, or fainting is a medical emergency — call for help.
act-air-sensitive: If you're unusually sensitive, take it easier on long or hard activity outside.
act-air-groups: Sensitive groups — asthma, heart or lung conditions, older adults, kids — should ease up outdoors.
act-air-inhaler: Keep quick-relief medication handy if you use it.
act-air-cutback: Cut back on time and effort outdoors.
act-air-windows: Keep windows closed; run an air filter if you have one.
act-air-mask: A well-fitting N95 or KN95 helps if you must be outside.
act-air-indoors: Stay indoors with windows closed if you can.
heat-guide-caution: Caution: fatigue is possible with prolonged time outside or activity. Take breaks, find shade, and drink water.
heat-guide-xcaution: Extreme caution: heat cramps and heat exhaustion are possible. Limit strenuous activity, rest in shade, and hydrate often.
heat-guide-danger: Danger: heat exhaustion is likely and heat stroke is possible with prolonged exposure. Avoid exertion, stay somewhere cool, and check on neighbors.
heat-guide-xdanger: Extreme danger: heat stroke is highly likely. Avoid being outside, seek air conditioning, and check on vulnerable neighbors.
context-top-hot: The hottest location in the network right now.
context-top-bad: The worst in the network right now.
context-rank-hot: {n} of {total} locations are hotter right now.
context-rank-bad: {n} of {total} locations are worse right now.
yesterday-same: About the same as this time yesterday.
prov-confirmed: Confirmed: calibrated against a reference monitor.
prov-provisional: Provisional: not yet calibrated against a reference monitor.
prov-derived: Combined from this area's heat and air readings.
compare-same: {a} and {b} are about the same right now.
compare-provisional: One or both readings are provisional (not yet calibrated), so this is a rough comparison.
alerts-note: Alerts update only while this page is open — there is no background push or account.
alert-line: {place}: {param} is now {reading} — at or past your alert level of {threshold}.
alert-provisional: This reading is still provisional (not yet calibrated), so treat it as rough.
notify-body: Now {reading} — at or past your alert level of {threshold}.
watch-intro: Set a level for this measurement. While this page is open, you'll see an alert here when this location reaches it. Saved on this device only — no account, no server.
watch-number-label: Alert at this reading or higher
watch-need-value: Enter a number to alert at first.
notify-granted: On-device notifications are on for this browser.
notify-blocked: Notifications aren't on — the in-page alerts still work.
copy-fail: Couldn't copy — copy the address bar instead.
brief-done: Summary copied — paste it into an email, a flyer, or testimony.
brief-source: Source: swelter community sensor network — open data (CC0).
brief-network: Copy a summary of the whole network
brief-network-done: Network summary copied — paste it into an article, a report, or testimony.
heat-band-note: The shading is a coolest-to-hottest cue only — the number on each marker is the exact reading, in your chosen units.
exp-level-minimal: Minimal — little added heat or air stress
exp-level-high: High — limit time and exertion outdoors
legend-value-note: This measurement is shown by its value on each marker, not by a severity category. Higher numbers mean more of the pollutant; see the List or Table view for every location.
what-is-aqi-body: The Air Quality Index (AQI) turns a pollution concentration into a 0–500 scale and a named category. Higher is worse: 0–50 is Good, 100+ starts to affect sensitive people.
aqi-usg: Unhealthy for sensitive groups — AQI 101 to 150
aqi-window: The AQI shown is computed from each location's hourly mean, not a 24-hour average.
provisional: Provisional locations have only early, uncalibrated readings — still being double-checked, and never shown as a confirmed category. Status is conveyed by text and pattern, not color alone.
exp-note: Heat + air exposure combines the heat index and the PM2.5 AQI into one level (Minimal to Extreme), taking the higher of the two and flagging when heat and air are both elevated. It is decision-support, not a validated health index, and never a claim that conditions are safe.
how-to-read: How to read this — and what it does not say
trust-summary: Confirmed readings are calibrated against a reference monitor and carry a ± uncertainty. Provisional readings are early and uncalibrated. This page reports what the air and heat readings are; it does not tell anyone they are safe. Use it alongside how you feel and official advisories.
footer-data: Observations are public domain (CC0-1.0). Download the full history — no account, no key.
footer-note: Each reading carries its calibration state and, when calibrated, a published uncertainty.
no-data: No data yet. Run `swelter demo --serve` or `make demo`.
